turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

**What the training set says about the top decile (>19 %):**
- Almost all record recipes are **mixed‑cation, mixed‑halide Pb absorbers** (FAMAPbBrI / CsFAMAPbBrI) — wide‑enough grains, suppressed halide segregation, ~1.55–1.6 eV gap.
- **n‑i‑p with a low‑defect, well‑aligned ETL** (SnO₂‑c/np, or TiO₂‑c|TiO₂‑mp) **plus an interfacially passivated HTL contact** dominates: e.g. `HS‑Ph‑CN | Spiro` 19.6, `SrCl₂ | Spiro` 20.8, `CH₃O‑PEIA | Spiro` 22.05, `OAI | DM` 22.9. The common denominator is an *added dipole/passivation layer or a superior arylamine HTL at the perovskite/HTL interface*, which kills the dominant recombination channel in n‑i‑p cells.
- In p‑i‑n, the winners are **C60|BCP with a hole‑selective polymer/SAM (PTAA, 2PACz) and Cu** (18.9–20.3), because PTAA/SAM removes the PEDOT:PSS energy‑level mismatch (‑5.0 eV vs. ‑5.2/‑5.4 eV needed) and Cu/C60‑BCP gives a low‑resistance, non‑reactive cathode. PEDOT:PSS‑based p‑i‑n devices cap out near 15–16 %.
- Penalized: Sn/Bi/Sb/Ge absorbers, pure Br or pure‑Cs wide‑gap, HTL‑free carbon back contacts, PEDOT:PSS, flexible PET/PEN substrates, mesoporous drop‑infiltration.

**Candidate screening:**
- **c019** FAMAPbBrI | TiO₂‑c|mp | **DM** | Au. DM is the dopant‑free spiro‑type HTL that in the training set appears in the single best cell (OAI|DM, 22.9). Deep HOMO (~‑5.3 eV), no Li‑TFSI/tBP hygroscopic dopants → clean interface, high V_OC. Best pick.
- **c079** FAMAPbBrI | SnO₂‑np | **CsPbBr₃‑np | Spiro** | Au. All‑inorganic perovskite‑nanocrystal interlayer = graded band alignment + halide‑rich passivation of surface Pb traps on the best ETL/HTL pair (SnO₂‑np/Spiro cluster gives 19–22 %).
- **c085** CsFAMAPbBrI | C60|BCP | **PTAA | PFN‑Br** | Cu (p‑i‑n). Exactly the top p‑i‑n motif in training (PTAA/Cu → 20.1, 18.15, 18.35) with an extra PFN‑Br dipole layer to improve hole extraction and wetting; Cs‑containing triple cation for phase stability.
- **c061** CsFAPbI | **SnO₂‑c | C60‑SAM** | Spiro | Au. A fullerene self‑assembled monolayer on SnO₂ passivates oxygen‑vacancy/hydroxyl traps and removes the ETL/perovskite conduction‑band offset — the classic recipe for >21 % FA‑rich narrow‑gap cells.
- **c062** FAMAPbBrI | **SnO₂‑np | PCBM‑60** | Spiro | MoO₃|Au. Bilayer ETL (inorganic + fullerene) suppresses interfacial recombination and hysteresis; MoO₃ buffer keeps the Au contact ohmic. Training analogues (SnO₂‑c|SnO₂‑np, TiO₂‑c|PCBM) sit at 19–19.1 %.

Close runners‑up: c059 (SnO₂‑QDs/Spiro), c015 (2D EPA capping), c055 (SWCNT|Spiro), c093/c089 (PTAA p‑i‑n).

**Final: c019, c079, c085, c061, c062**
